--- title: "The parser layer" --- Every ESPN wrapper can return either the **raw JSON `Dict`** ESPN ships or a **tidy DataFrame** produced by the parser layer. This guide shows both, side by side, executed at build time. ## `return_parsed` — raw `Dict` vs tidy frame For parser-backed ESPN wrappers, `return_parsed=True` is the **default**, so you get a polars frame out of the box. Pass `return_parsed=False` to recover the raw payload. ::: {#b4b20ce9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_team_roster raw = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13, return_parsed=False) # -> Dict print("raw payload type:", type(raw).__name__) print("top-level keys:", list(raw.keys())[:10]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` raw payload type: dict top-level keys: ['timestamp', 'status', 'season', 'athletes', 'coach', 'team'] ``` ::: ::: The same call with the default `return_parsed=True` gives a tidy frame: ::: {#aa38c8ad .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = espn_nba_team_roster(team_id=13) # -> polars.DataFrame (default) print("parsed frame:", df.shape) df.columns[:16] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` parsed frame: (17, 68) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['id', 'uid', 'guid', 'first_name', 'last_name', 'full_name', 'display_name', 'short_name', 'weight', 'display_weight', 'height', 'display_height', 'age', 'date_of_birth', 'debut_year', 'links'] ``` ::: ::: ## `return_as_pandas` — one frame, two engines The package is polars-first but pandas-friendly. Because the cache key excludes `return_as_pandas`, a single stored frame serves both callers — the conversion happens on read. ::: {#0e463ab3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} from sportsdataverse.nba import espn_nba_teams pl_frame = espn_nba_teams() # polars pd_frame = espn_nba_teams(return_as_pandas=True) # pandas print("polars type:", type(pl_frame).__name__) print("pandas type:", type(pd_frame).__name__) print("same row count:", pl_frame.height == len(pd_frame)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` polars type: DataFrame pandas type: DataFrame same row count: True ``` ::: ::: Quarto renders the pandas frame just as happily (note the `df-print: paged` styling from `_quarto.yml`): ::: {#f02a412d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} pd_frame[["team_id", "team_abbreviation", "team_display_name"]].head(5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
team_id team_abbreviation team_display_name
0 1 ATL Atlanta Hawks
1 2 BOS Boston Celtics
2 17 BKN Brooklyn Nets
3 30 CHA Charlotte Hornets
4 4 CHI Chicago Bulls
``` ::: ::: ## Sibling-API parsers compose explicitly NHL and MLB have their own native APIs whose wrappers return raw `Dict` and pair with a named parser you apply yourself. The shape is `parse_((...))`: ```python from sportsdataverse.nhl import nhl_web_pbp, parse_nhl_web_pbp df = parse_nhl_web_pbp(nhl_web_pbp(2023030417)) # 331-row polars frame ``` ::: {.callout-note} The parser contract is universal: empty/malformed payloads return a **zero-row frame** (not an exception), so you can chain without null-checks, and columns are snake-cased. See [Architecture](../architecture.qmd) for the full picture. :::
